children: Curve Finance and Yield Basis founder Michael Egorov wrote that onchain foreign exchange may develop from users’ currency-exchange and cross-border payment needs rather than being driven from the top down by banks and large financial institutions. According to Odaily, Egorov cited Brazil’s BRZ digital stablecoin and Monerium’s EURe as assets that support onchain exchanges and redemption into bank accounts. Keyrock data showed that onchain stablecoin trades involving emerging-market currencies were mainly between $1,000 and $10,000. Chainalysis data showed cross-border stablecoin activity exceeded $220 billion by mid-2026, up nearly 80% year over year. Egorov said the key challenge for onchain foreign exchange remains making liquidity economically sustainable; automated market makers can support markets for less-traded currencies by providing continuous liquidity and collecting trading fees. Banks are expected to remain important for fiat issuance, redemption and compliance, while moving funds onchain can reduce some traditional intermediaries.

title: Curve Founder Says Onchain FX May Be Driven by Real Payment Demand, Not Institutional Liquidity
